reports.title: Kodiak Gas Services Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results, Increases Full Year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA and Discretionary Cash Flow Guidance

guidance.heading: Full-Year 2026 Guidance
section: Kodiak is providing revised guidance for the full year 2026. The full year 2026 guidance below incorporates three quarters of the financial impact of the DPS acquisition given the April 1, 2026 closing date.

(in thousands, excluding percentages) | Low | High
Adjusted EBITDA (1) | 840,000 | 860,000
Discretionary cash flow (1)(2) | 580,000 | 600,000
Compression Infrastructure revenue | 1,255,000 | 1,275,000
Compression Infrastructure adjusted gross margin percentage (1) | 69.5 | 70.5
Power Infrastructure revenue | 100,000 | 120,000
Power Infrastructure adjusted gross margin percentage (1) | 65.0 | 70.0
Other Services revenue | 125,000 | 160,000
Other Services adjusted gross margin percentage (1) | 12.0 | 15.0
Maintenance capital expenditures | 80,000 | 90,000
Compression Infrastructure | 290,000 | 310,000
Power Infrastructure | 350,000 | 400,000
Total Growth capital expenditures | 640,000 | 710,000
Other capital expenditures (3) | 45,000 | 55,000
(2)Discretionary cash flow guidance assumes no change to Secured Overnight Financing Rate futures.

(3)Other capital expenditures guidance excludes a $42.6 million non-cash finance lease addition related to one of our operational offices. Although recognized in the second quarter of 2026 capital expenditures, this non-cash activity is not reflected in the investing section of our statement of cash flows and is therefore excluded from our full-year capital expenditures guidance.

desk.headline: Revenue up 24% to $402m, beat; record EBITDA, 2026 EBITDA and cash-flow guidance raised
results: Revenue rose 24% to $402m, helped by the new Power Infrastructure unit (the DPS deal) and 61% growth in Other Services.
Net income was $71.5m, or $0.70 a share (GAAP and adjusted the same), against a loss of $0.17 a year ago when one-off charges hit.
Compression fleet use was 98.3% and adjusted gross margin held at 70% for a third quarter; 102,000 hp of large units were added.
Free cash flow was negative $28m as growth capex reached $179m; debt was $2.8bn with leverage of 3.1x.
The dividend rose to $0.51 a share, and the buyback (about $31.7m left) was extended to end-2027.

guidance.summary: Kodiak lifted the bottom of its 2026 adjusted EBITDA and discretionary cash-flow ranges and cut power growth capex as equipment deliveries shift later.

points: Management pointed to repricing of existing compression contracts and firm pricing on new ones, mostly with escalators and longer terms.
Power deals under negotiation are mostly 10- to 15-year contracts, largely in Texas, with demand from data-centre developers.
Remote-monitoring technology helped offset higher lube oil costs, and lube oil prices are fixed for 2027.
Turbine deliveries run into 2028 and tight supply chains could slow capacity additions.
Management cautioned that further margin gains will be harder from current high levels.
call.source: Call coverage: KGS Q3 2026 deep dive — StockStory, 10 Nov 2026

watch: Progress on the 76 MW West Texas data-centre power project ahead of 2027 revenue.
Timing of power equipment deliveries and whether 2026 capex is cut further.
Free cash flow turning positive as growth spending eases.
